title: Add node-aware cross-model batching harness and stratified cold-start heatmap reporter
author: Maya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a new deterministic cross-model batching harness (node-aware) and a stratified cold-start heatmap reporter for benchmark lab visualizations. No API changes; internal test-only harness and reporters.
description:
Context and motivation:
We frequently see tail-latency regressions driven by cross-model packing decisions during multi-model serving (when short requests to smaller models are co-located with long KV-cache-heavy requests for larger models). Existing bench runners simulate per-model traffic in isolation and do not account for node-level contention when heterogeneous models are scheduled on the same GPU host. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a node-aware cross-model batching harness that can synthesize realistic co-location patterns and tune packing thresholds deterministically, and (2) a stratified cold-start heatmap reporter that visualizes cold-start penalty surface across priming lengths, model pairings, and placement topologies. Both are intended for the benchmark-lab suite (test-only, no production runtime change).

What this PR changes (high-level):
- New harness: bench/runners/node_crossmodel_batcher.go and bench/runners/node_crossmodel_batcher_test.go. The harness can load a YAML workload manifest that declares multiple model classes, sequence-length distributions, and node placement constraints. It simulates request scheduling and produces per-token latency traces annotated with model-id and node-id. Key features: deterministic random seed, pluggable packing heuristics (first-fit, size-aware-fit), and a throttling backpressure model to emulate kernel contention.
- New reporter: bench/reporters/coldstart_heatmap_reporter.py which consumes the harness traces and emits a compact heatmap CSV and an HTML preview. The reporter stratifies by (primer_length, model_pair, placement) and computes median/p95 cold-start penalty and the percent of requests experiencing >2x penalty.
- Small infra additions: bench/fixtures/crossmodel_examples.yaml (three canonical scenarios), a CI job definition bench/.github/workflows/bench-node-crossmodel.yml (bench-only workflow), and minor helper functions for trace serialization in bench/internal/trace_serializer.go.

Commits (summary):
- 6 commits total: initial harness skeleton; packing algorithms and deterministic scheduler; synthetic priming generator; trace serializer + test traces; heatmap reporter + CSV serializer; CI workflow and docs.

Files changed (high-level):
- bench/runners/node_crossmodel_batcher.go (+780 additions)
- bench/runners/node_crossmodel_batcher_test.go (+120 additions)
- bench/reporters/coldstart_heatmap_reporter.py (+210 additions)
- bench/fixtures/crossmodel_examples.yaml (+34 additions)

- Makefile targets: bench-run-crossmodel, bench-heatmap

Design notes and constraints:
- The harness intentionally runs deterministically by default (seed 42) so that performance regressions are reproducible across CI runs and developer machines.
- We model contention at the kernel occupancy level using a simple headroom model (available_tokens per-node) rather than attempting to reimplement GPU scheduling; this keeps the harness fast and tunable.
- Reporter output is intentionally compact CSV + a small self-contained HTML preview to make it easy to upload artifacts to CI and attach to PRs.
- No changes to production serving runtime or model artifacts. This lives entirely under benchmark-lab and is gated behind bench-only CI.

Checklist:
- [x] Bench harness implemented and unit-tested (bench/runners/*_test.go)
- [x] Reporter emits CSV and HTML preview with sample fixtures
- [x] Documentation added (docs/bench/node-crossmodel-batcher.md)
- [x] CI bench workflow added (does not run on main CI by default; bench-only)
- [x] Reviewed and addressed review comments below

Review conversation (abridged):
- Ethan Russo (review): "Nice isolated harness. Two asks: (1) can we parameterize the seed externally so CI can run deterministic and we can also re-seed for stress runs? (2) the heatmap bins are quite coarse for primer_length -- will we ever want continuous smoothing?"
- Maya Kapoor (reply): "Updated: seed is now exposed via CLI and env BENCH_SEED (default 42). Heatmap reporter now exposes a --smooth window to optionally apply simple moving-average smoothing; default is off to keep CSV raw."
- Priya Nair (review): "Concern: trace format compatibility with existing flamegraph pipeline. Can we add a codec shim?"
- Maya Kapoor (reply): "Added bench/internal/trace_serializer.go with codec v1 that supports translation to existing flamegraph JSON. Also added unit tests to validate roundtrip with small sample traces."
- Jonah Feldman (approval): "Approach looks good. Docs and examples are helpful for onboarding."

CI summary:
- bench-node-crossmodel.yml runs harness + reporter against the three fixtures and validates output CSV schema.
- First CI run failed due to a brittle timestamp ordering in test traces. Fixed in second commit by making timestamps monotonic in test fixtures.
- Final CI status: all bench jobs passed (reports attached to the run).

Performance notes (from local runs):
- In the canonical fixture (small model + large model co-located on one node), median cold-start penalty for the small model increases from ~12ms (isolated) to ~38ms when packed behind a long >1024-token request that primed the large-model KV cache. P95 exhibits larger amplification in several placement scenarios; the heatmap reporter makes these tradeoffs easy to scan.

Merge outcome:
- Merged to main via squash merge after approvals. Merge method: squash, merge commit created: bench: add node-aware crossmodel batcher + heatmap reporter (Maya Kapoor)
